iut_type: Whether a non-SIG-member brand owner can have SIG registration filed on their behalf by a SIG-member manufacturing subcontractor
customer_question: If we sell a Bluetooth product under our end-customer's brand, and the application and cost-bearing is handled by the manufacturing subcontractor (who is already a SIG member), is new SIG membership (Associate or Adopter) still mandatory for our end-customer if they haven't joined SIG themselves?
question_variants: Can a SIG-member manufacturer file and pay for a registration under a non-member brand owner's name?
Does the selling company itself need to be a SIG member, or is it enough that someone in the supply chain is a member?
actual_issue: The customer assumed that since the manufacturing subcontractor handling the registration logistics was already a SIG member, this might satisfy SIG's membership requirement even if the actual brand owner (the company whose name would appear on the product nameplate) had never joined SIG themselves.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG's own 'Do I Need to Qualify?' guidance states that to sell a Bluetooth product manufactured by yourself with your own name (or manufactured by another company but bearing your own name), the SELLING company must complete both SIG membership and the qualification/registration process. This requirement is independent of who actually files the application or pays the fees -- even if a SIG-member manufacturing subcontractor is willing to bear the cost and handle the application process entirely on the selling company's behalf, the registration still cannot be filed under the selling company's name unless that selling company is itself a SIG member. There is no workaround that allows a non-member brand owner to be registered using another company's membership status.
consultant_answer: Bluetooth SIG's rule is clear: the company shown on the product's nameplate (the selling company) must itself complete SIG membership and the qualification process, regardless of who files the application or pays the fees. Even if your manufacturing subcontractor (already a SIG member) is willing to bear the cost and handle the application on your end-customer's behalf, the registration cannot be filed under your end-customer's name unless your end-customer becomes a SIG member themselves.
decision_logic: When a customer asks whether a non-SIG-member brand owner can have registration filed on their behalf using a different company's (e.g., a manufacturing subcontractor's) SIG membership, the answer is always no -- the selling company whose name appears on the product nameplate must itself hold SIG membership, independent of which company actually performs or funds the application process.
final_recommendation: When a customer describes a registration scenario involving multiple companies (manufacturer, distributor, brand owner), explicitly confirm which company's name will appear on the product nameplate and verify that specific company's own SIG membership status, rather than assuming any SIG-member company in the supply chain satisfies the requirement.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer might attempt to register a product under a non-member brand owner's name using a manufacturing subcontractor's membership and cost-bearing, only to discover the registration cannot actually be completed that way, causing delays and requiring the brand owner to join SIG before proceeding.
